newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil gains whittled away by falling futures.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil gains whittled away by falling futures.

text.p: NWE gas oil continued its rollercoaster ride on the back of benchmark futures on Monday, soaring higher in the morning only to end the day lower as the recent IPE gas oil rally stalled in the afternoon.
Sept IPE gas oil ended $2.50 lower at $217.25 a tonne as dealers cleared out positions ahead of the contract's expiry on Thursday. The Sept/Oct spread ended at $8.00.
Traders said premiums on the physical market remained strong, buoyed by concerns over low stocks.
There was plenty of talk over low sulphur material with premiums assessed at Oct IPE +$17/+$19, cif Le Havre. No deals were reported.
"It's not so much there isn't any demand, just no one's offering," one trader said.
Demand for German heating oil was firm, with premiums talked at Oct IPE +$7/+$9.
A 38,000 tonne Russian cargo was also on offer at Sept +$2 cif NWE.
On the barge market, premiums were put at Sept IPE +$4/+$5 a tonne, but traders said buyers had been sidelined by the recent high outright price levels.
